source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Standard oxygen delivery requiring fairly little ongoing nursing monitoring once it has first been initiated for the client's plan of care","B":"Oxygen, like any medication, can cause adverse effects if given in excessive or insufficient amounts, requiring appropriate titration based on the client's specific needs","C":"Oxygen carrying essentially no risk whatsoever and requiring fairly little specific dosing consideration by the treating provider","D":"Oxygen delivery carrying fairly little established relationship to how well a client ultimately ends up doing clinically over the course of their care"}}
source_row.rationale: Oxygen is treated as a prescribed medication because, like any medication, it can cause adverse effects if given in excessive amounts (such as oxygen toxicity or, in certain COPD clients, reduced respiratory drive) or insufficient amounts (hypoxemia), requiring appropriate titration and ongoing monitoring based on the client's specific needs.
source_row.source_detail: Oxygen as a Titrated, Prescribed Therapy
source_row.source_name: AARC — Oxygen Therapy Clinical Practice Guideline
